options.text: Writing application business logic
Managing infrastructure through machine-readable, version-controlled files instead of manual clicks or ad-hoc commands
A type of container image
A registry for storing servers

questions.explanation: IaC defines and manages infrastructure through version-controlled files, making it repeatable, reviewable, and recoverable.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between declarative and imperative infrastructure?

options.text: Declarative lists the steps; imperative lists the end state
Declarative describes the desired end state and is idempotent; imperative specifies the ordered steps you run yourself
They are the same
Imperative is always safer

questions.explanation: Declarative definitions state the goal and let the tool reconcile to it (safe to re-apply); imperative definitions script the exact steps and order.

questions.prompt: How should secrets be handled in IaC?

options.text: Commit them in plain text so they are versioned
Keep them out of the files and store them in a secrets manager, referencing them instead
Email them to the team
Bake them into the base image

questions.explanation: Configuration lives in code, but secrets must not sit in plain text in the repo; store them in a secrets manager (or platform secret mechanism) and reference them.

questions.prompt: When a live system diverges from its defined desired state, that gap is called configuration ______. (one word)
questions.explanation: Configuration drift happens when manual, out-of-band changes make the running system differ from its definitions; declarative IaC and GitOps detect and correct it.

options.text: A way to write Dockerfiles
An approach where Git is the source of truth and an agent continuously reconciles the live system to match it
A Git hosting service
A container runtime

questions.explanation: In GitOps the desired state lives in Git; an automated agent reconciles the system to match, so changes are made via pull requests and drift is auto-corrected.

questions.prompt: Which are benefits of Infrastructure as Code? Select all that apply.

options.text: Repeatable environments from the same files
Changes reviewed through pull requests
Versioned, auditable history with easy rollback
It removes the need to ever test changes

questions.explanation: IaC makes infrastructure repeatable, reviewable, and auditable. Definitions still need testing — a bad definition can break infrastructure like bad code.
